title: dedicated-autoscaler-policy-flexible-burst-throttle-util-reporting
author: Ravi Desai
description: Implements a flexible burst throttle and improved utilization reporting for Dedicated autoscaler policies. Motivation: customers observed frequent short-duration bursts that caused overprovisioning and noisy utilization signals; this PR introduces a token-bucket based burst throttle with smoother decay, per-priority burst budgets, and end-to-end telemetry to make utilization and fallback decisions observable. The change includes policy logic in the autoscaler runtime, a new configurable policy schema for fleet and per-fleet overrides, migration hooks for existing policies, new dashboards and alert rules, and an integration test harness. Design notes: token-bucket smoothing uses an adaptive depletion window to reduce rapid on/off oscillation at the fleet level; priority buckets allow guaranteed throughputSLOs to reserve steady-state capacity while permitting short bursts for high-priority customers; utilization reporting now exports per-fleet and per-priority metrics and exposes a per-route 95th/99th burst usage metric. Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves existing tokenbucket settings unless new policy fields are set. See linked Linear tickets ENG-1284 and ENG-1299 for product requirements and acceptance criteria.

review_comments: Aisha Patel: Please add unit tests for the adaptive depletion window edgecases; currently coverage looks missing for negative refill rates.
Diego Morales: Can we add a short note on why we chose exponential decay vs linear? Concerned about long tail interactions with steady-state scheduling.
Karen Liu: Telemetry looks good. Suggest splitting per-priority metrics into a separate histogram to avoid cardinality issues.

Ravi Desai: Responding: added unit tests for depletion window and clarified exponential decay rationale in code comments and docs. Updated metrics to use histogram buckets and added a label guard on high-cardinality route tags.
Aisha Patel: Approved after tests fixed and small linter nits addressed.
ci_checks: integration-tests: fail on first run (timeout in autoscaler_integration), rerun: pass
release_notes: Dedicated autoscaler: add flexible burst throttle with token-bucket smoothing; per-priority burst budgets; new utilization metrics and dashboards; migration path preserves existing policies by default; recommend customers update fleet policies to opt-in to per-priority budgeting for improved cost efficiency.
performance_impact: Reduced 99th percentile burst-induced latency by ~15% in internal canary and decreased short-term overprovisioning cost by an estimated 6-9% on test fleets; telemetry enabled to quantify in production.
qa_notes: Integration tests cover steady-state and burst scenarios. Ran canary on two dedicated fleets for 48 hours with synthetic traffic patterns. Ops manually validated dashboard charts and alert firing. No customer-facing config changes required unless opting into new policy fields.
notes_and_followups: Follow-up work: expose per-customer budget dashboards in console (ENG-1305), add autoscaler controller autoscaling-policy e2e tests for multi-fleet scenarios, and a small perf-optimization to reduce metric scrape overhead (planned ENG-1312).
changelist_summary: Policy runtime additions, config schema bump, telemetry and dashboard assets, integration tests, docs and migration helper.
backport_plan: No immediate backport to older releases. If customers on pinned release request the fix, we will prepare a targeted backport with reduced surface area.
user_visible_changes: No API breaking changes. New policy fields are additive. Console users will see new dashboard tiles under Dedicated -> Autoscaler -> Throughput & Burst.
security_considerations: No new external surface. Metrics include only aggregated fleet and priority labels. Avoided route-level cardinality to prevent leakage.
approvals: Aisha Patel, Diego Morales, Karen Liu
